transcript:
>> This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Hundreds of thousands of people remain without electricity
after a powerful storm battered much
of the East Coast yesterday.
That same system also extended into parts of the Midwest.
NPR's Kat Lonsdorf reports roads flooded and hundreds
of flights were either delayed or canceled.
The storm was massive, stretching from Missouri
and Illinois into Massachusetts and all the way
down toward Georgia, bringing record flooding along the East
Coast and snow to parts of the Midwest.
It was a good day to stay inside and eat,
but it was a difficult day for many to cook,
with power knocked out for nearly a million customers.
Travel was also tough with more than 400 flights canceled
and more than 2,000 delayed around the country.
Flooding caused damage and disruption in many communities
with bridges and roads shut down.
The weather will be clearing up into the weekend,
hopefully making post-Thanksgiving journeys
for the tens of millions expected
to be traveling much smoother.
Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Washington.
>> President Trump's son-in-law and peace envoy,
Jared Kushner, says Russian President Vladimir Putin
has "shown restraint in the war against Ukraine
by not using nuclear weapons."
Kushner was speaking on a podcast hosted by the CEO
at the company that owns Politico.
Villa Marks reports.
>> On the "MD Meets" podcast with Axel Springer Chief,
Matthias Dovner, Kushner called Putin a grandmaster of politics
and credited him with holding himself back.
>> So far, Putin has showed restraint.
He's agreed not to use nuclear weapons,
which obviously is a big thing,
and he's reassured us that that's not his intention.
>> Kushner said he believes Putin wants peace
between Russia and Ukraine.
He also said peace talks should focus most of all
on ending the war, not deciding which side is right or wrong.
But this little sign of the war itself is winding down.
Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelenskyy
said in his nightly address to the nation Thursday
that Russia was preparing a new mass strike in the coming days.
For NPR News, I'm Villa Marks.
>> The Supreme Court is preparing to hear arguments
over the Trump administration's use
of third-country deportations.
NPR's Franco Ordonez reports.
>> Since taking office, President Trump has expanded
the controversial practice of deporting thousands of people
to countries where they have no ties.
Earlier this year, the Supreme Court said
Trump can temporarily resume the deportations,
which had been blocked by a lower court,
and scheduled oral arguments for next month.
Lawyers fighting the program argue
that many of these migrants are longtime residents
with no criminal history,
and that they face significant harm
being sent to third countries,
some that have records of torture and persecution.
The case carries significant implications
not only for Trump's immigration agenda,
but also for the broader scope of presidential power.
Franco Ordonez, NPR News.
>> This is NPR News in Washington.
New York City is getting ready
for the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade tomorrow morning.
Organizers pushed it back two days
because of a Thanksgiving storm that threatened
to make it unsafe to fly the giant balloons.
It's the first weather postponement
in the event's 100-year history.
The parade steps off at 830 Eastern Time
on Manhattan's Upper West Side
and ends at Macy's in Herald Square.
The share of the world's population
that's not affiliated with any religion
is expected to drop in the coming decades,
and PR's Jason DeRose has more on the findings
of a report from Pew Research.
>> About 2 billion people around the world
are religiously unaffiliated.
Pew says that number is expected to rise in most countries,
but researchers project that those increases will be offset
by an overall population drop in one country, China.
The change isn't about people becoming religious.
Rather, a very large portion of the population there
is religiously unaffiliated.
In the coming decades, China is expected to experience
a dramatic population decrease due to low birth rates.
>> Pew projects that the global population
of the religiously unaffiliated will drop from 24% to 17%
by the year 2070.
Jason DeRose, NPR News.
>> Supermarket chain Kroger has sent layoff notices
to corporate employees this week.
The company hasn't said how many workers
are affected in this round.
Kroger announced last month that it plans
to cut about 3,000 corporate jobs over three years
as it expands its use of artificial intelligence.
This is NPR.
>> Want to hear this podcast without sponsor breaks?
Amazon Prime members can listen to NPR News now,
sponsor free through Amazon Music.
Or you can also support NPR's vital journalism
and get NPR+ at plus.npr.org.
That's plus.npr.org.

topics.text: Storm with record flooding and snow disrupts East Coast and Midwest, leaves nearly a million without power
Jared Kushner says Putin has shown restraint by not using nuclear weapons in Ukraine war
Supreme Court to hear arguments on Trump administration's third-country deportations
Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York postponed two days due to storm, first in 100 years
Pew report projects religiously unaffiliated share of world population falling from 24% to 17% by 2070
Kroger sends layoff notices to corporate employees as part of planned 3,000-job cut
